items.title: Identify Common Factors for Whole Number Sizing
items.explanation: To find the size of square tiles that fit exactly into a rectangular room, the side length of each tile must be a factor (divisor) of both the length and the breadth. For example, in a 12 ft by 16 ft room, the common factors are 1, 2, and 4 feet. Since she wants to use as few tiles as possible, she should choose the largest possible side length, which is 4 feet.

items.title: Apply HCF to Minimize Packaging Bags
items.explanation: When dividing quantities into equal bags, the bag weight must be a common factor of both amounts. To minimize the number of bags, the bag weight should be the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of the two quantities. For 84 kg and 108 kg, the HCF is 12 kg, allowing for the fewest possible bags.

items.title: Use Prime Factorization to Simplify HCF
items.explanation: For larger numbers with many factors, prime factorization simplifies finding the HCF. By breaking down each number into its prime components (e.g., 84 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 7 and 108 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3), you can easily identify the common prime factors to determine the HCF without listing all divisors.
